claims.claim: No new facts, numbers, capabilities, or time references were introduced

claims.claim: scan.txt's 'HARD VIOLATIONS: 3' (NEG-PARALLEL) reflect real violations in the rewritten text
claims.evidence: The three flagged NEG-PARALLEL substrings ('it's not just', 'not just a form to fill out; it's', 'more than just') all occur inside the change-summary's illustrative quotation of the ORIGINAL sentence being removed (result.md line 21), not in the live rewritten body (lines 1-13). The scanner does not distinguish quoted-for-illustration text in the summary from the actual rewritten prose, so this scan output is a false positive as applied to expectation 3.

claims.claim: NO-COPULA and CHALLENGES-FORMULA patterns were also fixed (beyond the expectations list)

uncertainties: Source draft had garbled grammar (missing articles/prepositions) throughout; executor treated this as an artifact of eval construction rather than a literal-preservation signal and produced grammatical output.

The Speed/Clarity/Confidence list was kept as a de-bolded three-item list (passing the RULE-OF-3 load-bearing test) rather than collapsed to prose; executor flagged this as a defensible alternative reading if the grader expected prose.
needs_review: The VAGUE-ATTRIB retention-rate claim was deleted rather than replaced; a human with an actual source may want to re-add it with citation.

suggestions.reason: scan.txt's AI-tell scanner scans the entire result.md file, including the change-summary section, and flags illustrative quotations of the REMOVED source phrases (e.g., the NEG-PARALLEL quote describing what was cut) as if they were live violations in the rewritten text. This produced 'HARD VIOLATIONS: 3' and multiple pattern hits (INFLATION, VAGUE-ATTRIB, DIDACTIC, GENERIC-CLOSER, AI-VOCAB, ING-ANALYSIS) that do not actually exist in the rewritten body -- all of them trace to quoted-for-illustration text in the change summary. Anyone relying on scan.txt's summary line without reading result.md directly would wrongly conclude this arm failed. Consider having the scan tool scan only the rewritten-text portion (before the '---' separator) when a change summary is present, or have executors keep illustrative quotes out of the change summary.

suggestions.assertion: The rewritten text contains no generic positive closer...
suggestions.reason: The body's final sentence ('Onboarding is the foundation of lasting customer relationships.') is still a fairly stock B2B-marketing closing claim, even though it isn't the specific 'future looks bright' cliche the assertion names. This one passes on the letter of the assertion but a stricter version of this check (e.g., flagging any generic value-proposition restatement as a closer, not just forward-looking-optimism phrasing) would be more discriminating for future runs.

eval_feedback.overall: All 8 expectations pass on genuine merit -- the rewritten body is clean of every targeted pattern, the change summary correctly names 8+ stable IDs, and no facts were fabricated. This confirms the 'Full rewrite' vs 'Edit with constraints' disambiguation fix worked for this prompt (previously scored 4/8 for suppressing the change summary; this run correctly produced both rewrite and summary). The one real gap is in the eval harness itself: scan.txt's naive substring scan over the whole file conflates the change summary's illustrative quotes of removed text with the live rewrite, producing misleading 'HARD VIOLATIONS' that a grader must manually discount by reading result.md directly.
